newsitem.title: USA: Dlr to steal thunder from EMU-diluted mark-Experts.
newsitem.headline: Dlr to steal thunder from EMU-diluted mark-Experts.

text.p: The dollar has more thunder to steal from a mark weakened by prospects of a watered-down Euro, experts predicted on Monday.
"The strength is coming from dollar/mark," said Chase Securities technical analyst John Tirone, who commented on the other casualty of the French general elections -- the mark.
"The sell-off on the mark crosses certainly are the result of the dollar's strength against the mark," Tirone added.
The Socialist Party won on a platform opposing the fiscal austerity needed to meet the Maastricht Treaty debt criteria.
Tirone said the mark caved in against all the crosses -- including the French franc that suffered a brief setback past the key 3.3835 level on the French elections results.
"Dollar/mark broke through some big resistance levels," Tirone said, noting dollar/mark led trading.

Dollar/mark took out a strong resistance at 1.7120, or the 62-percent retracement from a high of 1.7389 on April 28 to a low of 1.6680 May 12, to breath through 1.7210. At 1500 EDT/1900 GMT, dollar/mark was quoted at 1.7304/09.
"A close above 1.7270 would be pretty positive," Tirone predicted.

"We should see a move to 1.7389 marks, the year high, and then, a move to at least 1.7440," added Tirone, who pointed out the dollar's relative weakness in May "was never negative. The mark always was in a trading range and never broke out of it."
Tirone said the dollar's strength against the mark pressured the German currency on all fronts.

"Mark/yen had really good support at 67.40 and that's gone. The question is 'Where can the mark find additional support?'" the Chase analyst asked. "The 67.30 area is what you want to watch. The pressure is going to be there."
Mark/Swiss slipped as well, nearing the year's lows.
"You can see the dollar's strength is pressuring all the crosses. On sterling/mark, we are looking at 2.83 marks and then, we are starting to move to a very big level, 2.8325," Tirone also said.

The 2.8325 level on sterling/mark is a target in the move up from recent lows in the 2.7140/2.7420 area. Breaking that level without a temporary pullback to 2.8125 would point to an attack on 2.8575, analysts said.
"These are very, very significant levels. To be able to have these gyrations (on the crosses) up here is bullish for the dollar," Tirone concluded.
Ben Morden, analyst at the consultancy firm I.D.E.A., agreed the dollar has enough momentum to score more gains against the mark.

"It looks dollar/mark can go to the cycle high of 1.7389 pretty quick," Morden said. "The mark is doing poorly against the non-EMU (Euroepan Monetary Union) currencies, and doing poorly as well against the other EMU European currencies."
Many analysts hold the view that watered-down debt criteria for the countries allowed to join the Euro on the scheduled on January 1, 1999, would pressured the mark as well as the German debt.
Morden predicted the loss of any major support on any of the mark crosses -- including on the much-watched mark/Paris -- could result in all-around weakness for the German unit.
Senior analyst Scott Siller at MCM CurrencyWatch agreed "the obvious next for dollar/mark is 1.7390, the high on April 28. Dollar/mark is sloping higher."
Siller acknowledged dollar/Swiss is somewhat lagging the move, indicating the strength is focused on dollar/mark.
"New highs on dollar/mark do not necessarily mean that dollar/Swiss or dollar/yen are going to new (recent) highs," Siller pointed out.

"What really distorts the picture is mark/Paris where the move above 3.3835 after the elections may be seen as a false break up. You could see a big trading range there until the market figures out the situation.
